hypothesis: A structured, AI-specific crisis playbook combined with scripted war-game exercises will lead cross-functional executive teams to respond to large-scale AI incidents faster, with fewer harmful actions and better regulatory-appropriate communication, than teams using a generic operational incident playbook without AI-specific guidance.

baseline.description: Generic operational incident management playbook with no AI-specific decision rules, metrics, or escalation structures.
playbook_assets: Standard major-incident runbook used for IT outages and cyber incidents (PDF or wiki).
Existing RACI chart for enterprise incidents (no AI-specific roles).
Generic communications templates for service outages and cyber events.
Standard incident-logging form in the firm’s incident management tool.

process_characteristics.detection_rules: Generic service-availability, latency, and system error-rate alerts only.
process_characteristics.governance: Incident commander from IT/operations; ad-hoc involvement of risk, compliance, and business lines.
process_characteristics.communication: Single generic press/regulator template; no pre-defined AI-risk disclosures.
process_characteristics.decision_rights: Model shutdown/escalation not explicitly defined; treated like any technical component.
process_characteristics.forensics: Standard log collection; no AI-specific model, data, or decision-trace capture.

treatment.description: AI-specific crisis management playbook aligned with Chapter 13, including detection cues, governance roles, communications templates, and post-incident processes, exercised via scripted war-games.
playbook_assets: AI-incident classification guide distinguishing AI-driven crises from normal incidents.
AI-specific RACI matrix: roles for Chief AI Officer / CDAO, CRO, CISO, business heads, and board committees.
Decision trees for model throttling/shutdown, customer remediation, and market-coordination steps.
AI-incident communications templates for regulators, investors, media, and employees.
Data and forensics checklist for AI failures (model artifacts, prompts/inputs, training data snapshots, logs).
War-game scenario scripts and injector events tailored to AI failures in financial services.

process_characteristics.detection_rules: Additional AI-specific indicators such as abnormal model drift, decision anomalies, correlated errors across models, and conduct-risk spikes.
process_characteristics.governance: Pre-defined AI crisis cell with explicit escalation to relevant board committee based on materiality.
process_characteristics.communication: Segmented templates for supervisors, markets, and customers emphasizing AI-risk context, remediation, and safeguards.
process_characteristics.decision_rights: Explicit authorities for pausing or constraining AI models, and for moving to manual or alternative processes.
process_characteristics.forensics: Structured collection of AI-specific artifacts and a pre-agreed minimal set of explainability outputs.

workloads.name: W1-credit-approval-spiral
workloads.description: Simulated large-scale AI misclassification in retail/SME credit approvals leading to widespread wrongful declines and liquidity impacts.
workloads.scenario_type: Firm-level customer-impact crisis with potential conduct and reputational risk.

inputs.ai_failure_pattern: Regime shift in applicant characteristics causing model to under-approve specific segments.
inputs.regulator_profile: Retail banking supervisor in highly consumer-protective jurisdiction.
pre_configured_alerts: Spike in auto-declines vs historical baseline.
Increased complaint rate on digital channels.
Drop in portfolio approval rate beyond tolerance.

phases: Phase 0 – Briefing: 5–10 minutes overview, starting metrics, and roles.
Phase 1 – Detection: 20–30 minutes; anomalies emerge via simulated dashboards and injects.
Phase 2 – Containment: 30–40 minutes; decisions on pausing models, customer messaging, and manual overrides.
Phase 3 – External Communication: 30 minutes; regulator and media queries arrive via injects.
Phase 4 – Debrief: 30–40 minutes; performance metrics captured and discussed.

workloads.name: W2-trading-algo-feedback-loop
workloads.description: Simulated autonomous AI-driven trading strategy enters a destabilizing feedback loop, amplifying market volatility and creating potential systemic concerns.
workloads.scenario_type: Market and systemic-risk crisis with coordination needs across infrastructures.

inputs.ai_failure_pattern: Reinforcement learning trader overreacts to short-term signals, triggering self-reinforcing price swings.
inputs.regulator_profile: Market regulator overseeing trading venues and high-frequency trading.
pre_configured_alerts: Order-to-trade ratio spikes for AI-driven strategies.

phases: Phase 0 – Briefing: 5–10 minutes; role assignment including market relations and treasury.
Phase 1 – Detection: 15–20 minutes; unusual market behaviour, alerts from venues.
Phase 2 – Containment: 25–35 minutes; decisions on circuit breakers, algo throttling, and risk limits.
Phase 3 – Coordination: 20–25 minutes; simulated interactions with exchanges, central counterparties, and regulators.
Phase 4 – Debrief: 25–30 minutes; performance review and systemic-risk discussion.

workloads.name: W3-generative-ai-misconduct
workloads.description: Simulated misuse or malfunction of generative AI in customer communications causing misleading or non-compliant advice at scale.
workloads.scenario_type: Conduct, regulatory, and reputational crisis affecting multiple business lines.

inputs.ai_failure_pattern: Prompt-injection-like pattern leading to biased or inaccurate advice for a vulnerable segment.
inputs.regulator_profile: Conduct authority focused on mis-selling and vulnerable customers.
pre_configured_alerts: Spike in chat-handovers to human agents around specific products.
Keyword-based detection of problematic advice in logs.

phases: Phase 0 – Briefing: 5–10 minutes; roles include head of customer, legal, compliance.
Phase 1 – Detection: 20–25 minutes; emergent patterns from QA logs and complaints.
Phase 2 – Containment: 30–35 minutes; decisions on disabling features, issuing corrective guidance, and remediation offers.
Phase 3 – Communication: 20–25 minutes; simulated regulator/media attention and internal staff comms.
Phase 4 – Debrief: 20–30 minutes; root-cause framing and conduct-risk implications.

randomization.unit_of_randomization: executive crisis-response teams (cross-functional groups of 6–10 people)
randomization.assignment: Teams are randomly assigned to either Baseline or Treatment condition for each workload, with counterbalancing across multiple runs so each team eventually experiences both conditions in different scenarios.
randomization.stratification: Optional stratification by prior incident-management experience to balance expertise across conditions.

blinding.participant_blinding: Teams are told they are evaluating crisis response approaches but are not explicitly informed which playbook is the AI-specific treatment vs the generic baseline.
blinding.observer_blinding: Independent scorers assessing metrics receive anonymized logs and artefacts without knowledge of whether they originate from Baseline or Treatment sessions.

standardization.inject_schedule: Identical sequence and timing of scenario injects for Baseline and Treatment runs of the same workload.
standardization.information_set: Same underlying data feeds, dashboards, and external queries; only the playbook, roles, and templates differ.
standardization.time_limits: Fixed time windows for each phase across conditions to ensure comparability.
standardization.team_composition: Each team includes representatives (or role-players) for business, risk, technology, operations, communications, and legal/compliance where possible.

metrics.name: time_to_ai_crisis_recognition
metrics.description: Elapsed time from first anomaly alert/inject to explicit recognition and verbalization that this is an AI-driven crisis with AI-specific implications.

metrics.name: time_to_decisive_containment_action
metrics.description: Elapsed time from first anomaly alert/inject to first clearly documented decisive containment action (e.g., model throttling, kill switch activation, switching to manual process).

metrics.name: harm_exposure_index
metrics.description: Scenario-specific proxy index for potential customer, market, or conduct harm remaining at simulation end, based on pre-defined mapping from team decisions to quantitative exposure scores.

metrics.name: regulatory_readiness_score
metrics.description: Expert-rated score of how regulator-ready the team’s notifications, disclosures, and remediation plans are, based on a standardized rubric.

metrics.name: coordination_effectiveness_score
metrics.description: Observer-rated effectiveness of cross-functional coordination and role clarity during the incident.

metrics.name: communication_consistency_score
metrics.description: Degree of consistency between internal and external messages across channels (staff, regulators, media, customers) as assessed by independent reviewers using a rubric.

metrics.name: data_and_forensics_completeness
metrics.description: Proportion of required AI-specific data and evidence artefacts that the team identifies, requests, and logs during the exercise.

metrics.name: playbook_adherence_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of critical steps in the relevant playbook (generic or AI-specific) that the team executes within the timeline.

metrics.name: participant_confidence_delta
metrics.description: Change in self-reported confidence in managing AI crises from pre-exercise to post-exercise survey.

metrics.name: post_mortem_actionability_score
metrics.description: Quality and concreteness of structural improvement actions proposed in the post-incident review.

primary.criterion: Median time in the Treatment condition is at least 25% lower than in the Baseline condition across workloads, with statistically significant difference under a non-parametric paired test where applicable.
Mean harm_exposure_index in the Treatment condition is at least 20% lower than in the Baseline condition for each workload, controlling for team differences.

secondary.criterion: Average regulatory_readiness_score is at least 2 points higher (on 0–10 scale) in Treatment than Baseline.
Treatment teams achieve at least 80% completeness on average, and at least 15 percentage points higher than Baseline.
Treatment teams show statistically higher scores than Baseline with fewer conflicting or ad-hoc messages.
Treatment teams produce more actionable and AI-specific structural fixes, with mean score at least 1.5 points higher than Baseline.

exploratory.criterion: Treatment sessions produce a greater positive shift in confidence than Baseline sessions while not masking recognition of residual gaps (i.e., no overconfidence spikes).

failure_modes.name: non_comparable_sessions
failure_modes.description: Differences in facilitator behaviour, inject timing, or available information across Baseline and Treatment sessions compromise comparability.
mitigations: Script facilitator prompts; use a detailed inject playbook.
Use a facilitator checklist and audio/video recording to audit adherence.
Run pilot sessions and refine to reduce variance.

failure_modes.name: insufficient_sample_size
failure_modes.description: Too few teams or sessions lead to inconclusive differences between conditions.
mitigations: Plan multiple runs per workload with different teams.
Use within-team crossover designs where teams experience both conditions on different days/workloads.
Treat results as formative if statistical power is low and document this explicitly.

failure_modes.name: role_mismatch_or_underpowered_teams
failure_modes.description: Teams lack critical roles (e.g., no risk or communications representation), skewing outcomes.
mitigations: Pre-define minimal role set; enforce through invitations and attendance checks.
Allow trained observers to ‘role-play’ missing functions using pre-briefed constraints.

failure_modes.name: gaming_or_hindsight_bias
failure_modes.description: Participants reuse knowledge from earlier runs or treat exercises as puzzles rather than realistic simulations.
mitigations: Vary scenario specifics across runs while keeping structural difficulty constant.
Rotate teams and clearly emphasize realism and behavioural authenticity in the briefing.
Use debriefs to surface and correct unrealistic assumptions.

failure_modes.name: measurement_bias
failure_modes.description: Observers scoring outputs may unconsciously favour one condition.
mitigations: Use anonymized, time-stamped artefacts for scoring.
Train multiple scorers and measure inter-rater reliability.
Resolve scoring discrepancies via predefined rules.

failure_modes.name: tooling_complexity_overwhelms_participants
failure_modes.description: Dashboards or simulators are too complex for non-technical executives, confounding performance with usability issues.
mitigations: Pilot interfaces with representative executives and simplify iteratively.
Provide a brief, standardized dashboard walkthrough before each run.
Ensure both conditions use tools of comparable complexity.

core_libraries: fastapi or flask (for lightweight web dashboards, optional)

infrastructure.runtime: Local machines or a shared server; no internet access required once dependencies are installed.
infrastructure.data: Synthetic, non-sensitive data sets for credit portfolios, trade flows, customer interactions, and incident logs.
interfaces: Web-based or notebook-based dashboards presenting anomaly timelines and key risk indicators.
Console or web UI for facilitators to trigger scenario injects and track phase timings.

personnel.participants: Cross-functional executive or senior-management teams (6–10 people per team).
personnel.facilitators: At least one trained facilitator per session to run injects and manage time.
personnel.observers: 1–3 observers per session to log decisions, timestamps, and qualitative behaviours.

governance_and_safety.data_protection: Use only synthetic or fully anonymized data in the repository; no production data.
governance_and_safety.psychological_safety: Set norms emphasizing learning over performance evaluation; avoid individual blame.
governance_and_safety.regulatory_sensitivity: Ensure scenarios are clearly labeled as simulations and not forecasts or representations of specific institutions.

run_instructions.title: Set up repository and dependencies
details: Clone the GitHub repository: `git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/boardroom-blind-spots.git`.
Navigate to the crisis-simulation module, e.g., `cd boardroom-blind-spots/experiments/chap13_crisis_mgmt`.
Create and activate a Python virtual environment.
Install dependencies: `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

run_instructions.title: Generate synthetic data and baseline scenarios
details: Run the data-generation script: `python generate_synthetic_data.py --workload all`.
Verify that synthetic datasets (credit portfolios, trades, chat logs) are created in the designated `data/` directory.
Optionally inspect sample records to ensure realism and to brief facilitators.

run_instructions.title: Configure playbooks and conditions
details: Open the configuration file `config/experiment_config.yaml` (or equivalent).
For each workload (W1, W2, W3), ensure that both `baseline` and `treatment` playbook paths are correctly specified.
Assign team IDs and conditions (Baseline/Treatment) in `teams_config.yaml`, following the randomization and counterbalancing plan.

run_instructions.title: Start the facilitator console and dashboards
details: Launch the facilitator console: `python run_facilitator_console.py`.
Launch participant dashboards: `python run_dashboard.py --workload W1` (using different ports or URLs for each team/session).
Verify that anomaly indicators and base metrics display correctly before participants enter.

run_instructions.title: Conduct pre-exercise briefing and surveys
details: Brief participants on objectives, roles, and ground rules without revealing which condition they are in.
Distribute and collect pre-exercise surveys to measure baseline confidence and perceived readiness.
Assign explicit roles (incident lead, risk lead, tech lead, comms lead, etc.) following the appropriate playbook.

run_instructions.title: Run the simulation phases with scripted injects
details: Start the workload (e.g., `python run_simulation.py --workload W1 --team_id TEAM_A --condition baseline`).
Use the facilitator console to trigger injects (alerts, regulator calls, media queries) according to the standardized schedule.
Observers log key decisions, timestamps, and references to playbook use in structured observation forms.
Adhere strictly to time budgets for each phase; announce transitions clearly.

run_instructions.title: Collect artefacts and run post-exercise surveys
details: Export all session logs, decision timelines, and communication drafts to the `results/` directory with unique session IDs.
Collect completed post-exercise surveys from participants to compute `participant_confidence_delta` and qualitative feedback.
Save facilitator and observer notes in structured formats (e.g., JSON or CSV) that reference session IDs.

run_instructions.title: Score performance and compute metrics
details: Run the scoring script: `python score_sessions.py --results_dir results/`.
Provide anonymized artefacts to independent scorers for rubric-based metrics (e.g., regulatory_readiness_score).
Review automatically computed metrics (e.g., time_to_decisive_containment_action, harm_exposure_index) and validate a sample for accuracy.
Export consolidated metrics to `analysis/metrics.csv` for statistical comparison.

run_instructions.title: Analyze differences between baseline and treatment
details: Use the analysis notebook `analysis/compare_conditions.ipynb` (or a Python script) to compare Baseline vs Treatment for each metric and workload.
Apply simple statistical tests (e.g., Wilcoxon signed-rank for paired data, Mann-Whitney U for independent groups) where sample size permits.
Generate plots (boxplots, time-series, radar charts) summarizing performance differences for governance audiences.

run_instructions.title: Conduct qualitative debrief and identify structural fixes
details: Facilitate a structured debrief using a standardized guide aligned with section 13.8.
Document proposed structural improvements, mapping them to governance, process, technology, and culture domains.
Store debrief outputs under session-specific directories to feed into the `post_mortem_actionability_score` rubric.

timeline_events.timestamp: ISO 8601 datetime or relative seconds from start
